questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Similar healthcare system, able to communicate with patients and colleagues.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Challenging. Clinical placement plan was finalized shortly before departure. Reliable and expedient communication with coordinator was lacking at times. Difficult to obtain information about when and where to report on the first day. Had a meeting with my coordinator at the host university on the Friday before beginning clinical rotations where I was informed that parts of the plan had fallen through and alternatives needed to be pursued; this was a bit stressful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Meeting scheduled in advance with coordinator at host university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of chaos but the coordinator was kind and tried to be helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Challenging and unintuituve; I struggled doing this on my own and suggest asking the coordinator to walk you through the registration process at your meeting.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Impossible to describe. 
Also, I'm not even sure if registration is strictly necessary when enrolled for only clinical rotations?

questions.answer: Not much because email correspondence with coordinator was sporadic at times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not applicable; clinical rotations only.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask your coordinator if and how you should register at the host university when enrolled for clinical rotations!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really engage in any of the non-academic opportunities. I think you have to actively seek out these opportunities when only enrolled for clinical rotations since you're not automatically included in the welcome/introduction for exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The student union (SiO) and the hospital (OUS) offer affordable gym memberships and other activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the great outdoors surrounding Oslo; go hiking in the area or skiing if you're into that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Outdoorsy stuff like hiking (Frognerseteren, Sognsvann, Voksenkollen and Grefsenkollen are very local, shorter walks) and skiing. Ø-hopping in Oslo fjord during the summer. Go on a hyttetur for a long weekend. Visit the local museums; I recommend Nobel Fredssenter and Nasjonalmuseet, even if the new building is a bit imposing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Must be actively sought out; join the facebook group for med students at UiO

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None come to mind

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Oslo is fantastic.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Follow up with your coordinator early on and repeatedly.
I recommend doing 4 placements of 3 weeks each. 
Prioritize departments/medical specialties and have back-up options; the clinical rotations might not be locked in despite written confirmation.
Enjoy Oslo!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be a real struggle to gain access to the hospital's patient record system.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining extra clinical experience in medical specialties I hadn't been assigned to during earlier rotations at home university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Can be a bit exhausting repeatedly being new at different departments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
